original_question: For a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i in the filtration between the sum-of-squares cone Σ_{n+1,2d} and the cone P_{n+1,2d} of positive semidefinite forms, explicitly describe its dual cone C_i^∨ = {L in Hom(R[X], R) | L(f) ≥ 0 for all f in C_i}.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Open Problem 2: “Give an explicit description of C_i^∨.” In the paper this is posed specifically for a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i in the distinguished filtration of cones between Σ_{n+1,2d} and 𝒫_{n+1,2d}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target: it correctly focuses on one of the paper’s distinguished strictly separating cones C_i and asks for an explicit description of its dual cone, which is exactly Open Problem 2 in Section 3.2. It also correctly situates C_i between the SOS cone Σ_{n+1,2d} and the PSD cone 𝒫_{n+1,2d}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))
missing_details: The ambient dual space should be the finite-dimensional dual Hom_R(ℱ_{n+1,2d},R)=ℱ_{n+1,2d}^*, where ℱ_{n+1,2d} is the real vector space of homogeneous forms of degree 2d in X=(X_0,…,X_n), not the much larger Hom(R[X],R). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

To be stand-alone and paper-faithful, C_i should be identified as the specific cone C_i:=C_{V_i} from the lexicographic Veronese filtration, not an arbitrary intermediate cone. The paper defines C_W by the Gram-map condition and then sets C_i:=C_{V_i}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

The setup n,d∈N, k=binomial(n+d,n)-1, the lexicographic ordering of I_{n+1,d}={α∈N_0^{n+1}:|α|=d}, and the monomials m_j(X)=X^{α_j} are implicit in your draft but needed to identify the paper’s exact C_i. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

The definitions of H_i and V_i are omitted: H_i={[z]∈ℙ^k | ∃x∈ℂ^{n+1}:(z_0,…,z_{n+i})=(m_0(x),…,m_{n+i}(x))} and V_i is its Zariski closure in ℙ^k. These are the varieties from which the cones C_i are built. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

The phrase “strictly separating intermediate cone” should be made explicit as Σ_{n+1,2d} ⊊ C_i ⊊ 𝒫_{n+1,2d}. If one wants the paper’s index-level characterization, equation (6) gives the strict ranges in non-Hilbert cases: for n≠2, the strict cones begin at C_{n+1}; for n=2, they begin only after C_{n+1}=Σ_{n+1,2d}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

Your draft does not mention that Section 3.2 uses the fact that every C_i is closed, so that (C_i^∨)^∨=C_i and the original filtration can be studied via the reverse dual filtration. This is part of the immediate nearby context for Open Problem 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))

The neighboring “homogeneous truncated moment problem” interpretation of C_i^∨ is a separate Open Problem 3, so it should not be folded into the refined question unless explicitly requested. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))
refined_question: Let n,d∈N, let ℱ_{n+1,2d} be the real vector space of homogeneous degree-2d forms in X=(X_0,…,X_n), and set k:=dim(ℱ_{n+1,d})−1=binomial(n+d,n)−1. Order I_{n+1,d}:={α∈N_0^{n+1}:|α|=d} lexicographically as α_0,…,α_k, put m_j(X):=X^{α_j}, define q_A(Z):=ZAZ^t for A∈Sym_{k+1}(R), and let 𝒢:Sym_{k+1}(R)→ℱ_{n+1,2d} be the Gram map 𝒢(A)=q_A(m_0(X),…,m_k(X)). For 0≤i≤k−n, define H_i:={[z]∈ℙ^k | ∃x∈ℂ^{n+1}:(z_0,…,z_{n+i})=(m_0(x),…,m_{n+i}(x))}, let V_i⊂ℙ^k be the Zariski closure of H_i, and set C_i:=C_{V_i}={f∈ℱ_{n+1,2d} | ∃A∈𝒢^{-1}(f): q_A|_{V_i(R)}≥0}. Assume that C_i is a strictly separating cone in the filtration Σ_{n+1,2d}=C_0⊆⋯⊆C_{k−n}=𝒫_{n+1,2d}, i.e. Σ_{n+1,2d}⊊C_i⊊𝒫_{n+1,2d}. Give an explicit description of the dual cone C_i^∨:={L∈Hom_R(ℱ_{n+1,2d},R) | L(f)≥0 for all f∈C_i}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 2, not Open Problem 1 or 3. The key phrase “explicitly describe its dual cone” matches the paper’s official wording almost verbatim. The nearby context in Section 3.2 explains that the authors are studying the reverse dual filtration because each C_i is closed, and then immediately pose Open Problem 2 for a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i. Open Problem 3, which asks for a homogeneous truncated-moment interpretation of C_i^∨, is presented as a separate follow-up problem rather than as an equivalent reformulation, so the refined question should stay narrowly on the explicit description of C_i^∨ itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06468))
